chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, by his chain to Mani' ibn Hajjaj, from Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Muskān, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

I heard Aba 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Verily, Allah has assigned four thousand angels to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), disheveled and covered with dust, until the Hour rises. They accompany those who visit him, visit him when he is ill, and attend his funeral when he dies.
ai.seo_question: Who are the angels assigned to the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the cosmic significance of Karbala by noting that four thousand angels, described as 'shuuthan ghubran' (disheveled and dusty), have been assigned to honor Imam al-Husayn’s grave until the Day of Resurrection. This perpetual angelic attendance underscores the unique spiritual status of the Imam’s resting place, transforming the act of Ziyarah into a celestial event where angels accompany visitors, visit the Imam in his 'illness' (a common Shia theological concept regarding the Ahl al-Bayt), and witness his funeral. This tradition reinforces the belief that the grave of the Imam is a focal point of divine mercy and angelic service, bridging the earthly and heavenly realms.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. My father narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān Al-Naysābūri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad Al-Yamāni, from Manī’ (ibn Ḥajjāj), from Ziyād, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad Al-Ḥalabi, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: Verily Allāh has dedicated four thousand angels to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) who are disheveled and covered with dust until the rising of the Hour. These angels accompany everyone who goes to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.), visit them if they become ill, and attend their funerals when they die.
